lessons.title: Determine the Area of Trapezoids
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a trapezoid using the formula A = ½(b1 + b2) × h.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words trapezoid, base, height, and area.

concept.heading: How do we find the area of a trapezoid?
concept.intro: A trapezoid is a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides. The two parallel sides are called the bases, and they have different lengths.
concept.keyIdea: Area of Trapezoids. Formula: Area = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h. 1. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape with one pair of parallel bases. 2. Add the two bases together: (b1 + b2). 3. Multiply by the perpendicular height, then take half

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My trapezoid window has a top base of 4 feet, a bottom base of 8 feet, and a height of 5 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
I add the bases first: 4 + 8 = 12.
I multiply by the height: 12 × 5 = 60.
I take half: ½ × 60 = 30. So the area is 30 square feet.
linesEs: Mi ventana trapezoidal tiene una base superior de 4 pies, una base inferior de 8 pies y una altura de 5 pies.
Escribo la fórmula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h.
Sumo primero las bases: 4 + 8 = 12.
Multiplico por la altura: 12 × 5 = 60.
Tomo la mitad: ½ × 60 = 30. Entonces el área es 30 pies cuadrados.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller trapezoid: bases 3 cm and 5 cm, height 2 cm.
First, what is 3 + 5? Yes, 8.
Next, what is 8 × 2? Yes, 16.
Now take half: ½ × 16 = 8, so the area is 8 square centimeters.
linesEs: Ahora un trapecio más pequeño: bases de 3 cm y 5 cm, altura de 2 cm.
Primero, ¿cuánto es 3 + 5? Sí, 8.
Luego, ¿cuánto es 8 × 2? Sí, 16.
Ahora toma la mitad: ½ × 16 = 8, así que el área es 8 centímetros cuadrados.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a trapezoid. Formula: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h.
vocabulary.example: A = 1/2(b₁ + b₂)h

vocabulary.definition: A four-sided shape with just one pair of parallel sides.
vocabulary.example: A table top wider than the bottom shelf — the top and bottom edges are parallel, the two sides slant inward

vocabulary.definition: Two lines or sides that stay the same distance apart and never meet.
vocabulary.example: The top and bottom of a parallelogram never get closer together — matching arrowheads (›) mark one parallel pair, double arrowheads (››) mark the other.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two parallel sides of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.example: If the bottom of the trapezoid is 10 ft, then b₁ = 10 ft in the formula A = ½(b₁ + b₂) × h

vocabulary.definition: The other parallel side of a trapezoid.
vocabulary.example: If the top of the trapezoid is 6 ft, then b₂ = 6 ft; both bases are parallel to each other

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance between the two parallel sides.
vocabulary.example: A dashed vertical line from the top base straight down to the bottom base at a 90° angle — NOT the slanted side

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.example: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.example: A trapezoid with b₁ = 10, b₂ = 6, h = 4 has area = ½(10 + 6) × 4 = 32 sq units

vocabulary.definition: Break a figure into simpler shapes.
vocabulary.example: A trapezoid = a rectangle + 2 triangles.

vocabulary.definition: A trapezoid with two square corners.
vocabulary.example: One side stands straight up from the base.

lessons.title: Apply Area Concepts to Solve Problems
lessons.objective: I can find the area of a composite figure by decomposing it into basic shapes, including a regular polygon split into triangles, and adding or subtracting the areas.
lessons.languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words composite figure, decompose, add, and subtract.

concept.heading: How do we find the area of a composite figure?
concept.intro: A composite figure is a shape made of two or more simple shapes joined together. We decompose it into basic shapes, find each area, then add or subtract.
concept.keyIdea: Area of Composite Figures. 1. Decompose: Split the irregular shape into basic figures (rectangles, triangles, trapezoids). 2. Calculate: Find the area of each individual sub-figure. 3. Combine: Add the areas together (or subtract if a piece is removed/cut out)

worked.title: Watch me
lines: My L-shaped room splits into two rectangles: one is 12 ft by 8 ft, the other is 6 ft by 5 ft.
First rectangle: A = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 square feet.
Second rectangle: A = 6 × 5 = 30 square feet.
The pieces are joined, so I add: 96 + 30 = 126.
So the total area is 126 square feet.
A regular polygon splits the same way: a stop sign is a regular octagon, so I cut it into 8 congruent triangles that meet at the centre.
One triangle has a base of 14 9/10 inches and a height of 18 inches, so A = 1/2 × 14.9 × 18 = 134.1 square inches.
There are 8 congruent triangles, so I multiply instead of adding eight times: 134.1 × 8 = 1,072.8 square inches.
linesEs: Mi cuarto en forma de L se divide en dos rectángulos: uno de 12 pies por 8 pies, el otro de 6 pies por 5 pies.
Primer rectángulo: A = largo × ancho = 12 × 8 = 96 pies cuadrados.
Segundo rectángulo: A = 6 × 5 = 30 pies cuadrados.
Las partes están unidas, así que sumo: 96 + 30 = 126.
Entonces el área total es 126 pies cuadrados.
Un polígono regular se divide igual: una señal de alto es un octágono regular, así que la corto en 8 triángulos congruentes que se unen en el centro.
Un triángulo tiene una base de 14 9/10 pulgadas y una altura de 18 pulgadas, así que A = 1/2 × 14.9 × 18 = 134.1 pulgadas cuadradas.
Hay 8 triángulos congruentes, así que multiplico en vez de sumar ocho veces: 134.1 × 8 = 1,072.8 pulgadas cuadradas.

together.title: Let's try together
lines: Now an L-shape made of a 5 ft by 4 ft rectangle and a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangle.
First rectangle: 5 × 4 = 20 square feet.
Second rectangle: 3 × 2 = 6 square feet.
Are they joined or cut out? Joined, so we add: 20 + 6 = 26 square feet.
linesEs: Ahora una figura en L formada por un rectángulo de 5 pies por 4 pies y otro de 3 pies por 2 pies.
Primer rectángulo: 5 × 4 = 20 pies cuadrados.
Segundo rectángulo: 3 × 2 = 6 pies cuadrados.
¿Están unidos o recortados? Unidos, así que sumamos: 20 + 6 = 26 pies cuadrados.

vocabulary.definition: The total space inside a figure made of basic shapes. Formula: A = A₁ + A₂ — add the parts (or subtract a missing piece).
vocabulary.example: Total area = area of rectangle 1 + area of rectangle 2.

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.example: An L-shaped room = a 12×8 rectangle joined to a 6×5 rectangle; total area = 96 + 30 = 126 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: To break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes.
vocabulary.example: Draw a dashed line across the L-shape to split it into two rectangles — now you can find each area separately

vocabulary.definition: Add up the areas of the smaller shapes to get the total.
vocabulary.example: T-shaped hallway: top rectangle = 30 sq ft, bottom rectangle = 28 sq ft → total = 30 + 28 = 58 sq ft

vocabulary.definition: Take away the area of a missing piece from a bigger shape.
vocabulary.example: A 14×10 pool with a 6×4 cutout: 140 − 24 = 116 sq ft of water surface

vocabulary.definition: A math rule written with symbols.
vocabulary.example: Rectangle: A = l × w; Triangle: A = ½ × b × h; use the right formula for each piece of a composite figure

vocabulary.definition: A shape whose sides are all the same length and whose angles are all the same size.
vocabulary.example: A stop sign is a regular octagon.

vocabulary.definition: Exactly the same size and shape.
vocabulary.example: The 8 center triangles of a regular octagon all match.

title: Festival Floorplan

Compare the trapezoid to a rectangle with the average base length.

create: Sketch a festival floor with a trapezoid and a rectangle. Label enough measurements to find its area, then show a second valid decomposition.

support.prompt: What is the area of a trapezoid with bases 6 cm and 10 cm, and height 4 cm?
feedback: 24 is 6 × 4 — only one base was used. Add both bases first: 6 + 10 = 16.
40 is 10 × 4 — only the longer base. A trapezoid uses the average of BOTH bases.
64 is (6 + 10) × 4 without the ÷ 2. Take half of the bases' sum before multiplying by the height.
hints: A trapezoid has two bases (6 cm and 10 cm) plus a height (4 cm) — all three belong in the formula.
Use A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h: add the bases first, then multiply by the height, then take half.
Add 6 + 10 to get the base sum, multiply that by 4, then cut the result in half.

support.prompt: A trapezoid has an area of 45 sq ft, bases of 7 ft and 11 ft. What is the height?
feedback: Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 3 = 27, not 45. Double the area first: 2 × 45 = 90, then ÷ 18.
Check it: (7 + 11) ÷ 2 × 10 = 90 — that's double the area. Divide 90 by 18, not by 9.
hints: You already know the area (45 sq ft) and both bases (7 ft and 11 ft) — the height is what's missing.
Simplify first: ½ × (7 + 11) = 9. So the equation becomes 45 = 9 × h.
Divide 45 by 9 to find the height in feet.

support.prompt: What is the first step when finding the area of a trapezoid?
choices: Subtract the shorter base from the longer base
support.explanation: The formula is A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. The first step is to add the two parallel bases.
feedback: The two bases get ADDED, not multiplied — they are the parallel lengths the formula averages.
Subtracting tells you how much longer one base is, not the combined length the formula needs.
The divide-by-2 comes later, applied after the bases are combined — the first move gathers both bases.
hints: Look at the trapezoid formula A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h. Parentheses show what happens first.
Ask what (b₁ + b₂) means: are the two parallel bases combined by adding, multiplying, or subtracting?
Say the formula in words: 'half of (base one ___ base two) times height.' The word that fills the blank is your first step.

support.prompt: A trapezoid has bases of 5 in and 9 in, and a height of 6 in. What is its area?
feedback: You used addition; use multiplication and division.
Try ½ × 9 × 5 step by step.
Triangle formula uses ½ × base × height.
hints: Circle the two bases (5 in and 9 in) and the height (6 in) — the trapezoid formula uses all three.
Follow A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h in order. Skipping the ½ makes your answer come out doubled.
Compute 5 + 9 = 14 first, then multiply 14 × 6, and finally take half of that product.

steps: Read the blueprint: A trapezoid-shaped patio stone has b1 = 4 ft, b2 = 8 ft, and h = 6 ft.
Write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h
Add the bases, then multiply by height: (4 + 8) × 6 = 12 × 6 = 72
State the area: A = 72 sq ft
support.explanation: The student forgot to multiply by ½, so their answer is double the true area. The correct area is A = ½ × (4 + 8) × 6 = ½ × 72 = 36 sq ft, not 72 sq ft.
hints: Compare the last step to the formula A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h — what operation is missing?
The student found (b1 + b2) × h, which is the area of a whole parallelogram made from two trapezoids. One trapezoid is only half of that.

support.prompt: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
support.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
feedback: Double both sides: area × 4.
Double one side: area doubles.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.

support.prompt: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
support.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
feedback: A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
Test: same perimeter, different areas?
Perimeter does not determine area.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.

support.prompt: Find the area of an L-shape made of a 5×3 rectangle and a 2×4 rectangle.
feedback: A thin shape can have big perimeter, small area.
Area and perimeter are not linked.
You must use both to describe a shape.
hints: Two rectangles make this L: one is 5 × 3 and the other is 2 × 4.
Joined pieces mean you add their areas after computing each one with length × width.
Find 5 × 3, then 2 × 4, and add the two products together.

support.prompt: When should you subtract areas instead of adding them to find the area of a composite figure?
choices: When one shape is larger than the other
When a piece is cut out or removed from a larger shape
support.explanation: Subtract when a piece is removed from a larger shape (like a window cut from a wall). Add when two shapes are joined together (like an L-shape).
feedback: Overlap is different — subtracting is for a piece removed.
Size alone doesn't decide — subtract only when part is removed.
Not always — you add pieces that are joined together.
hints: Think of real examples: a window in a wall versus two rooms joined into an L-shape.
Ask for each choice: is material missing from the shape, or are pieces being combined?
Picture a wall with a window: you can't paint the glass, so its area comes OFF the wall's area. Match that idea to a choice.

steps: Identify the shapes: An L-shaped room is made of two joined rectangles: 8 ft × 5 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft.
Find each area: First rectangle = 8 × 5 = 40 sq ft. Second rectangle = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft.
Combine the areas: Total = 40 × 12 = 480 sq ft.
support.explanation: The two rectangles are joined, so add their areas — do not multiply them. Total = 40 + 12 = 52 sq ft.
hints: Look at the last step. When two pieces are joined, do you add or multiply their areas?
Joined pieces are added: 40 + 12 = 52 sq ft, not 40 × 12.

support.prompt: Predict the area for these settings. Give the answer in square units. Round to four decimal places if needed.
support.explanation: (10 + 4) × 6 ÷ 2 = 42. Average the two parallel bases, then multiply by perpendicular height.
hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.
Use the relationship you explored in Investigate. Check with a second method.

support.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel bases 10 m and 6 m, and perpendicular height 4 m. Find its area in square meters.
support.explanation: Average the bases: (10 + 6) ÷ 2 = 8. Multiply by height: 8 × 4 = 32.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.
Draw a model or write the relationship first. Check your answer in the original situation.

steps: Read the blueprint: A trapezoid window has b1 = 7 ft and b2 = 13 ft. The slanted side measures 10 ft, and the straight-up height between the bases is 6 ft.
Write the formula: A = ½ × (b1 + b2) × h
Substitute values: A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 10
Calculate: A = ½ × 20 × 10 = 100 sq ft
core.explanation: The student used the slanted side (10 ft) as the height instead of the true perpendicular height (6 ft). The height in the trapezoid formula must be measured straight up between the two bases, not along the slanted side. The correct area is A = ½ × (7 + 13) × 6 = ½ × 20 × 6 = 60 sq ft, not 100 sq ft.
hints: Look at which measurement was used for h. Is it the straight-up distance between the bases, or the slanted edge?
The height must form a right angle with both bases. A slanted side is longer than the true height and will make the area too big.

steps: Identify the shapes: A 16 ft × 9 ft floor has a 4 ft × 5 ft supply closet cut out of one corner. Find the usable floor area.
Find the large rectangle area: A = 16 × 9 = 144 sq ft.
Find the cutout area: A = 4 × 5 = 20 sq ft.
Find the usable area: Usable area = 144 + 20 = 164 sq ft.
core.explanation: The closet is cut out, so subtract its area instead of adding it. Usable area = 144 − 20 = 124 sq ft.
hints: Look at the last step. The closet was removed from the floor — should its area be added or subtracted?
When a piece is cut out, subtract: 144 − 20 = 124 sq ft, not 144 + 20.

core.prompt: Predict the area for these settings. Give the answer in square units. Round to four decimal places if needed.
core.explanation: (11 + 4) × 6 ÷ 2 = 45. Average the two parallel bases, then multiply by perpendicular height.
hints: Identify which quantities the requested measure uses.
Use the relationship you explored in Investigate. Check with a second method.

core.prompt: A floor is a 6-by-4 rectangle joined without overlap to a triangle of base 6 and height 3. Find the total area.
hints: Name the given quantities and the quantity you need.

steps: Identify the bases and height: b₁ = 10 m, b₂ = 6 m, h = 7 m
Write the formula: A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h
Substitute values: A = ½ × (10 + 6) × 7
Calculate: A = (10 + 6) × 7 = 112 sq m
stretch.explanation: The student forgot to multiply by ½. A = ½ × 16 × 7 = ½ × 112 = 56 sq m.
hints: Look at Step 4. What happened to the ½?
The student skipped the ½ and just multiplied (b₁ + b₂) × h.

stretch.prompt: A trapezoid and a parallelogram both have a height of 8 ft. The trapezoid has bases of 5 ft and 11 ft. The parallelogram has a base of 7 ft. Which shape has the greater area? Explain your reasoning using the formulas.
stretch.frame: The trapezoid's area is ___ because ½ × (___ + ___) × ___ = ___. The parallelogram's area is ___ because ___ × ___ = ___. The ___ has a greater area by ___ sq ft.
stretch.explanation: The trapezoid's area is ½ × (5 + 11) × 8 = ½ × 16 × 8 = 64 sq ft and the parallelogram's is 7 × 8 = 56 sq ft, so the trapezoid is greater by 8 sq ft. Since both shapes share the height of 8 ft, the comparison really comes down to the trapezoid's average base, ½ × (5 + 11) = 8 ft, against the parallelogram's base of 7 ft.
hints: Both shapes share a height of 8 ft, so the real contest is between the base measurements.
Find each area with its own formula: trapezoid ½ × (5 + 11) × 8, parallelogram 7 × 8. Then compare the results.
Compute ½ × 16 × 8 for the trapezoid and 7 × 8 for the parallelogram, then subtract to say how much greater one is.

steps: Identify the shapes: Rectangle: 16 ft × 10 ft, with a 4 ft × 6 ft piece cut from the corner
Find the large rectangle area: A = 16 × 10 = 160 sq ft
Find the cutout area: A = 4 × 6 = 24 sq ft
Find total area: Total = 160 + 24 = 184 sq ft
stretch.explanation: Since the piece is cut out, subtract: 160 − 24 = 136 sq ft. When a piece is removed, subtract its area from the larger shape.
hints: Look at Step 4. Was the smaller rectangle added on or cut away?
The problem says the piece was 'cut from the corner,' so you should subtract, not add.

stretch.prompt: A T-shaped room can be decomposed in two different ways. Show both ways and prove they give the same total area. Use a T-shape where the top is 14 ft × 4 ft and the stem is 6 ft × 10 ft.
stretch.frame: Way 1: I split it into ___ and ___. Areas: ___ + ___ = ___. Way 2: I used a ___ rectangle and subtracted ___. Areas: ___ − ___ = ___. Both give ___ sq ft.
stretch.explanation: Way 1 splits the T into its two named rectangles: 14 × 4 = 56 plus 6 × 10 = 60, a total of 116 sq ft. Way 2 wraps the T in a 14 ft × 14 ft rectangle worth 196 sq ft and subtracts the two empty 4 ft × 10 ft corners, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft — the same region is being measured, so the decomposition you choose cannot change the area.
hints: The T's top slab is 14 × 4 and its stem is 6 × 10. Way 1 simply adds those two rectangles.
For Way 2, wrap the whole T in one big rectangle and subtract the empty corner rectangles.
Way 1: 14 × 4 plus 6 × 10. Then build the big rectangle for Way 2 and show the subtraction lands on the same total.
